phrasings.literal: Which tasks under the netcode snapshots campaign #273 were ready to start at the m1 tag?

gold_query: USE tags/m1 MATCH (t:task) WHERE t.unblocked AND t IN subtree(#273) RETURN t

trap.lure: writes USE tags/m1 ... WHERE t.ready, which is E302 because ready reads leases and markers that exist only at a branch tip; the fix the error names is t.unblocked

notes: README §7.6: at a past view the answer is the structural unblocked value. At tags/m1 (s42, SD §7) all of #274-#280 are open and #281 is cancelled (s39); SD §6 BLOCKS #274->#275, #274->#280, #275->#280, #276->#280, #276->#277 leave #274, #276, #278, #279 with no unfinished blocker; #273 is a container.

phrasings.literal: Thirty commits back on main, which tasks under the asset pipeline campaign #240 had been claimed and were in progress?

gold_query: USE main~30 MATCH (t:task) WHERE t IN subtree(#240) AND t.status = 'in_progress' RETURN t

trap.lure: tests t.claimed or t.lease (or runs leases()) under USE main~30; lease state is runtime and exists only at a tip, so the query fails with E302 instead of reading the historical status

notes: SD §11.6: main~30 is c.a11-discovered (s48). SD §7: #242 went open->in_progress with lease LS-242 at c.a2-claim (s27) and is still in progress; #241 (claimed s19, done s20) and #243 (done s28) are done; #245's claim is on lane/assets; #244, #901 and the rest of #240's subtree are open or cancelled.

phrasings.literal: Twenty commits back on main, what was the link state of the file docs/perf/results.md (#307)?

trap.lure: drops the past view and reads the current tree instead, reporting today's state of #307 as if it held twenty commits ago

notes: [50 §3.8]: link states are tree-derived and exist only at a branch tip with a resolved tree; at main~20 (c.filler-d7, SD §11.6) the binder refuses with E302 and no rewrite answers the question as asked (README §7.6). SD §9.3: at the tip #307 is replaced, which is the silent wrong answer.

phrasings.literal: How many commits does lane/net have that main has not received yet?

gold_query: CALL log(main..lane/net) YIELD commit RETURN count(*) AS commits

trap.lure: writes the range the other way round, log(lane/net..main), which counts main's commits that lane/net lacks

notes: SD §11.6: log(main..lane/net) lists lane/net's 9 own commits (the sync commit included, SD open point 5), and refs() gives lane/net ahead 9; log(lane/net..main) lists the 6 main commits c.gate-a7, c.filler-d11, c.lane-assets-pending, c.h2-prio2, c.run-net, c.filler-d13. A count over a range with filler commits is allowed (SD §16 item 13).

phrasings.literal: Which tasks under the audio mixer campaign #260 had their status changed on lane/audio in a way main has not picked up yet, and what were the old and new statuses?

gold_query: CALL diff(main...lane/audio, scope: #260) YIELD node, aspect, before, after, side WHERE aspect = 'status' AND side = 'theirs'

trap.lure: reverses the range (diff(lane/audio..main, scope: #260), or side = 'ours'), which lists main's changes since the common ancestor; main changed nothing under #260 after it, so the answer is empty (N05 only says the base is an LCA)

notes: SD §3.1: c.sync-audio absorbed main up to c.filler-d8, the LCA. SD §7: the lane side holds c.audio-b1-claim/c.audio-b1-done (#261 open->done), c.audio-b2-done (#262 open->done) and c.audio-b4-claim (#264 open->in_progress), all absent from the LCA; main's commits after s71 touch no node of #260's subtree. The two-dot main..lane/audio gives the same rows with N05 ([50 §2.4]).

phrasings.literal: As of store sequence number {{seq:c.a-r1-fix}} on main, list every direct dependency between two sections of the asset pipeline plan #254, as the dependent section and the section it depends on.

gold_query: USE s{{seq:c.a-r1-fix}} MATCH (s1:doc)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(s2:doc) WHERE s1.parent = #254 AND s2.parent = #254 RETURN s1, s2

trap.lure: names the section variables s1 and s2 next to a sequence-number revision; grammar v1 lexes s1 as an identifier outside revision positions, so the query is correct (the first revision's lexer failed with E001)

notes: SD §5.3 and §6: DEPENDS_ON #256->#255, #257->#256, #258->#257, #259->#258 and the shortcut #259->#255, all created by c.campaign-a (s4) and unchanged at c.a-r1-fix (s37); every section has parent #254. [50 §2.2] rule 4 makes s1 an identifier; the trap is defused, so the lured query returns the gold.

phrasings.literal: On main as it was 40 commits before its tip, which sections could the Rollout section #259 reach through some chain of two or more direct dependencies?

trap.lure: treats 'two or more' as shortest distance and drops #255 because #259 also depends on it directly (a NOT EXISTS on the direct edge), although the chain #259->#258->#257->#256->#255 has length 4

notes: SD §11.6: main~40 is c.review-a-r2 (s35); the DEPENDS_ON edges of SD §6 exist since c.campaign-a. Walks of length >= 2 from #259 reach #257 (2), #256 (3) and #255 (4, besides the direct shortcut), so all three qualify ([50 §3.7] rule 2).

phrasings.literal: Which commits have touched task #291, counting the one that created it?

trap.lure: types the id with a leading '#' in argv (lqb q history #291), which the shell reads as a comment, so the named call arrives without its required id and fails with a parameter error and the hint that '#' starts a shell comment

notes: SD §5.7: #291 was created by c.history and changed by c.h2-prio1, c.h2-label and c.h2-prio2; it has no edges (SD §6) and is a clean node (SD §11.6). Set order ignores repeated rows of one commit. [50 §6.1]-§6.2 rule 4: ids are bare in argv; 'id=#291' (# mid-token) would also arrive intact.
